title: Tenant fencing and surge patterns discovery - VeraGrid
summary: Early-stage discovery to understand VeraGrid's isolation requirements and surge handling. Main topics: reserved GPU sizing, tenant fencing (soft vs hard isolation), warm pool and prewarm strategies for 1k-3k qps spikes, SSO/KMS concerns, and a technical validation plan to run a 48-hour soak and two burst tests.

transcript:
Meeting: Tenant fencing and surge patterns discovery
Date/Time: 2026-04-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: 49m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (VeraGrid CTO), Lukas Meyer (Head of ML), Samir Acharya (Infra), Priya Rao (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:10] Anya: Hi, Anya Patel, CTO at VeraGrid. We run a clinical insights pipeline and evaluating how to serve real-time recommendations, th-thanks.
[00:20] Lukas: Lukas, head of ML. We're looking at moving from a batch-of-models to a low-latency online inference path, lots of spiky traffic.
[00:28] Maya: Awesome. Diego, do you want to say hi?
[00:31] Diego: Hey all, Diego Ramos, I'm the SE on this and will focus on perf, isolation, and validation.
[00:37] Samir: Samir, infra. on the call for tenancy and network requirements.
[00:41] Priya: Priya, security - SOC2, KMS, and legal touchpoints.

[02:15] Maya: Quick context — VeraGrid told us you need consistent latency at peak, but also isolation between tenants for PHI-sensitive customers, and a plan for big bursts — right?
[02:30] Anya: Yeah, exactly. We have multi-tenant traffic plus a handful of customers requiring dedicated isolation. We're evaluating if Redwood Hosted with dedicated pools or Private (VPC) makes sense. key constraints: 99th percentile < 120ms for short prompts, ability to burst up to 3x baseline for up to 10 minutes, and hard segmented tenancy for certain customers.

[05:00] Diego: Ok, a couple of levers we usually talk about: reserved GPUs for baseline throughput, warm pools / prewarm to reduce cold-start latency, and tenant fencing — which can be soft (scheduling + GPU tenancy isolation at the process level) or hard (separate node pools or physical isolation). Soft fencing is cheaper but has stronger noisy-neighbor risk.
[05:35] Lukas: What about model multiplexing? if we have smaller, faster variants for low-latency and a larger one for quality peaks, can Redwood roll to a cheaper fallback?
[05:50] Diego: Yes, we support model variants and automatic fallback by policy. You can route by latency SLO or cost threshold; during depletion we can route non-critical customers to quantized variants.

[08:00] Samir: On the dedicated side: we care about pinning workloads to GPU pools and ensuring veth/tenant fencing in the host kernel. For Private, we need VPC peering and HSM/KMS for keys. Is HSM in private deploy supported?
[08:20] Maya: For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via standard connectors; Hosted Dedicated also supports CMEK for enterprise. We'll share our KMS integration doc.

[10:45] Priya: SOC 2 artifacts? audit logs granularity, token-level tracing, retention policies — can we get sample logs?
[10:55] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC2 summary and an example audit log layout. note: some of the labels in our docs are shorthand, you may see typos like "KV cash" in a couple old notes — we'll clean those up.

[12:30] Diego: Let's talk numbers. Can you share baseline QPS and observed spikes?
[12:38] Lukas: Baseline is ~200 qps for our ensemble, but spikes hit ~1,000 qps for 3-5 minutes during morning syncs. we also have unpredictable bursts up to 3k qps during external events. Prompt lengths usually 32-128 tokens.
[13:00] Diego: That helps. So rough reserved sizing — you'd want enough reserved GPUs for baseline plus a sized warm pool for typical spikes. For 200 qps with your models (we estimated model A at ~8 tokens/sec/core), you'd start at N GPUs for baseline (we'll calculate exact in the sheet). For the 1k qps 5-min spike, warm pool + autoscale burst should cover it without dropping below latency SLO.

[16:00] Anya: Cost is the tricky part. If we reserve for baseline and then burst, what's the delta vs hosted on-demand?
[16:12] Maya: Reserved gives predictability: lower unit cost and guaranteed capacity. On-demand Hosted costs more per token at spike time, but avoids commit. We'll send a modeled scenario showing token-cost vs reserved amortization over expected usage.

[18:30] Lukas: For tenant fencing: we have two customers that must be fully isolated — no co-locating on same GPU. Is that possible in Dedicated?
[18:39] Diego: Yes — Dedicated pools can be configured for strict tenancy: single-tenant nodes for those customers, or soft isolation with cgroup and scheduler level fences. If you need legal proof we can set separate node pools and control scheduling; that's standard for PCI/PHI workloads.

[21:50] Samir: How fast is burst scaling? We need minutes-level recovery, not tens of minutes.
[21:58] Diego: For Dedicated, if you maintain a small warm pool prewarmed (we recommend 10-20% of expected peak), cold start is avoided. If we need to spin up more nodes, that's slower (minutes) depending on cloud provider; best practice is a warm buffer and queued prewarming during predictable windows.

[24:10] Maya: We have a spreadsheet template that models warm-pool size vs cost vs latency. I'll attach that.
[24:20] Anya: Great. Also, if a tenant is noisy, can we throttle at request level rather than evicting?
[24:29] Diego: Yes. Redwood has per-tenant rate limiting and priority-based queuing. You can rate limit and shape traffic to protect SLOs.

[27:00] Priya: On encryption: we need in-transit and at-rest with customer-managed keys for Private, and key-rotation logs. do you support key rotation hooks?
[27:12] Maya: Yes, rotation is supported and we surface rotation events in audit logs. We'll share the KMS integration checklist.

[30:00] Lukas: For validation plan — we'd like to do a 48-hour soak at baseline and two 10-minute synthetic bursts (1k and 3k qps) and run A/B quality checks. Can Redwood run the benchmarks inside Dedicated test pool?
[30:15] Diego: Absolutely. We can provision an isolated test pool in Dedicated or run in your Private environment if you prefer. We'll provide the benchmark harness and scripts. We'll also collect token-level latency and trace spans so you can see KV cache hit rates.

[33:40] Anya: One more: network egress and data residency — some customers require EU-only residency. Are regionally pinned Dedicated pools available?
[33:50] Maya: Yes, we can pin to region. For EU-only data residency we'd provision Dedicated capacity in the EU region and restrict routing.

[36:15] Samir: If we go with Hosted Dedicated, what's the fallback if capacity is exhausted during an unprecedented spike?
[36:25] Diego: Policy-driven fallbacks: route to compatible, lower-cost quantized model, or fall back to a best-effort on-demand pool. You can set hard limits to reject requests as well. We recommend a multi-tier fallback combining quantized variants and shedding non-critical traffic.

[38:40] Anya: Any gotchas with prewarming on GPUs for long prompt contexts? we have some prompts hitting 1024 tokens occasionally.
[38:50] Diego: Long contexts increase KV cache memory; kernel selection and sequence-length profiling matter. If 1024 tokens are common, we'll recommend different instance families or more memory-per-GPU configs; we'll call that out in the sizing sheet.

[41:05] Maya: I'll attach the pricing sketch and a link to the "burst modeling" sheet and the SOC2 summary.
[41:12] Maya: link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/burst-models/VERA-brief (placeholder)

[43:30] Priya: timeline: we need purchase decision by end of month, legal needs 2 weeks for contract review. if we go Private, lead time longer.
[43:40] Maya: Noted. We'll prioritize the security pack and a draft statement of work.

[45:50] Lukas: One operational question — what's the best practice for rolling model updates without impacting latency?
[46:00] Diego: Canary deploys and incremental traffic shift. Use hot KV cache warming on canary nodes and then tranche traffic. Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards and can auto-fallback during rollout regressions.

[48:10] Maya: Ok recap — action items and we'll reconvene for a technical deep dive next week. thanks everyone.
[48:20] Anya: Thanks all.

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-heard words and shorthand (e.g., "KV cash" seen in an internal doc reference) — please refer to attachments for canonical terms.
